Practical HP-TES integration constraints, such as acceptable refrigerant o charge increases and applicable suitable control strategies, are not discussed, while advanced control techniques are usually presented in simulation environments only. The literature lacks demonstrations of dual-mode HP-TES using single o room-temperature TES, specifically taking this concept from the design stage to the field test implementation stage Consequently, this research sheds light on the design, integration, modeling, control, experimentation, and field testing of a dual-mode single-room-temperature HP-TES. A framework for HP-TES system design was presented, and a dedicated supervisory controller was implemented. Page 15 of 127 DE-EE0009681 University of Maryland, College Park Project Objectives Statement of Project Objectives The objective of the project is to develop and validate an integrated 4-Ton (14.1 kW) heat pump-thermal storage system that can operate in both cooling and heating modes, capable of ≥50% peak demand reduction for 2 hours and ≥20% total energy efficiency improvement for all modes with the thermal battery at a cost of ≤$15/kWh . thermal The technology proposed herein consists of a dual-purpose (heating and cooling) thermal battery with room temperature storage integrated with heat pump(s) (HPs) for commercial applications. The battery serves as the heat reservoir, absorbing heat when operating as a condenser in cooling mode or rejecting heat when operating as an evaporator in heating mode. The value proposition of this project consists of: • Flexibility – using a single PCM at room temperature, the system may be used for both cooling and heating modes; • Efficiency – the room temperature PCM allows for reducing the cycle’s temperature lift, considerably increasing • Load Shifting – The thermal storage enables load shifting by leveraging the higher COP during on-peak hours, which will consequently result in cost. Scope of Work The project is divided into three phases, approximately one year each in duration: • Budget Period 1: Component and System Design, Prototyping, and Component Testing: The recipient will design a cost-effective thermal battery, begin the thermal battery prototyping, and run component-level tests. The recipient will conduct system-level modeling and design to establish the performance metrics and targets. • Budget Period 2: Full-Scale System Construction and Laboratory Testing: The recipient will build full-scale integrated heat pump-thermal storage systems. Two configurations (single and two heat pumps) are anticipated to be constructed. Each configuration will be tested, along with the baseline system, to establish reference performance values. • Budget Period 3: Field Testing and Validation: The recipient will conduct a field site test at a representative building.
